The web app’s `Plan` type has drifted from the API’s definition.

- Python accepts `free | pro | team | scale`.
- TypeScript accepts `free | pro | enterprise`.

So the newest tier—presumably `scale`—passes API validation but fails the web app’s closed-set validation because `scale` is absent from `packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts`. The reverse bug also exists: the web app recognizes `enterprise`, which the API rejects.

To prevent recurrence, define plans once and generate both the Python and TypeScript types from a shared contract—ideally OpenAPI or JSON Schema. Add a cross-language contract test and gate CI on new high-severity `crimes` findings. Manually maintained enums on both sides are what allowed this drift.

The route-drift findings are separate problems: one request uses `PUT` where the API declares `POST`, and another calls `/api/workspaces` when the backend exposes team-oriented routes. They can cause 405/404 failures, but they do not explain this validation error.
